clue.text: Bitter feud involving half the Italian city with soldiers surrounding a little policeman

indicators.note: only half the name of the city is kept, the rest of the word being dropped
the soldiers' letters stand around the little policeman, holding him inside

blocks.note: the first half of Venice
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers
DET is a short form of detective

explanation.surface: A feud in an Italian city where troops guard a junior police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged, bitter quarrel, classically a blood feud between families.

clue.text: Stop a second by the river

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
the Tay is Scotland's longest river

explanation.surface: Pausing briefly beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain or halt, as in staying put rather than moving on.

clue.text: Where youngster is laid to rest

definitions.text: Where youngster is laid to rest

blocks.note: surface reading: buried, as in a grave or funeral

blocks.clueFragment: Where youngster is laid to rest
blocks.note: setter's reading: where a baby is put down to sleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid to rest' suggests a burial; here the youngster is simply a baby being put down for a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A cradle is a small rocking bed in which an infant is put down to sleep.

clue.text: With short notice, prepare to give speech

blocks.note: an ad is a short form of advertisement, a public notice
to dress is to prepare, as with a salad or a wound

explanation.surface: Being asked at short notice to get ready to deliver a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal talk delivered to an audience, such as a public oration.

clue.text: Come together to defraud bank

blocks.note: to con is to swindle
a verge is a grassy bank or edge beside a road

explanation.surface: Accomplices meeting up to cheat a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or people that converge meet at a single point from different directions.

clue.text: Speaking with difficulty of total caught up in swindle

indicators.note: something caught up in a thing is trapped inside it, so the word for total sits within the swindle

blocks.note: utter means total, as in utter nonsense
a sting is a confidence trick

explanation.surface: Someone stammering because they are entirely embroiled in a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Total' looks like a noun (a sum) but works as the adjective, as in total or complete nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuttering is a speech impediment involving involuntary repetition of sounds.

clue.text: Long for direction, as lacking in courage

blocks.note: to crave is to long for
N for north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone yearning for guidance because they lack nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Craven means cowardly, contemptibly without bravery.

clue.text: Reinstated set order after upheaval

indicators.note: an upheaval throws things into disarray, so the letters are tossed into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: After a period of turmoil, order is re-established.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restored has been brought back to its former place or condition.

clue.text: Scoundrel lost his head -- the beast!

indicators.note: losing a head means the first letter of the word is removed

blocks.note: a rotter is a cad or scoundrel

explanation.surface: A villain beheaded, followed by a cry of 'the brute!'
explanation.walkthrough: ROTTER without its first letter leaves OTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is an animal, so it can be called a beast in the general sense of a creature.

clue.text: Sounds like little Edward is all of a whirl

indicators.note: the clue says outright that the word is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: Eddie is a pet form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Little Edward is in a spin.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirling circular current of water or air, a small whirlpool.

clue.text: Get tax I added included, as it can be traced back to another source

definitions.text: it can be traced back to another source
definitions.note: a description of a derivative thing, not a single word

indicators.note: items included are taken inside, so the tax and I go within the verb for get

blocks.note: to derive is to obtain or get from a source
VAT is value added tax, Britain's sales tax
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting a bill with tax included, plus a note about where it came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Added' reads as part of value added tax, but here it simply joins the I to the tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Something derivative is copied or developed from an earlier original work or substance.

clue.text: Suppress the way life unfolded

indicators.note: something unfolded is opened out and laid differently, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: Holding back the way one's life turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle is to smother or hold back, as in stifling a yawn.

clue.text: Do likewise to succeed with petition

blocks.note: to succeed someone is to follow them
a suit is a formal request or petition

explanation.surface: Copying others in order to win with a formal plea.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow suit is an idiom from card games meaning to copy what someone else has done.

clue.text: Textile worker becomes a police officer

blocks.note: serge is a hard-wearing twilled fabric
the ant is the crosswords' standard worker

explanation.surface: A mill hand changes careers and joins the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a rank in the police, above constable and below inspector.

clue.text: Set out to the shopping precinct for tools

indicators.note: set out here means laid out in a different order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a mall is a shopping centre
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: Heading off to the shops to buy some tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallets are wooden hammers, workshop implements for striking chisels or pegs.

clue.text: One of two groups making knitwear for women

blocks.note: a twin is one of a pair
sets are groups or collections

explanation.surface: Two groups of women knitting.
explanation.walkthrough: A twinset is a matching cardigan and jumper (sweater), a classic British women's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Twinsets are pairs of matching knitted garments, traditionally worn by women.

clue.text: Wanted teacher to be at the heart of the action

indicators.text: to be at the heart of
indicators.note: being at the heart of something puts it in the centre, inside the other word

blocks.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: Someone wanted a teacher to be central to events.
explanation.walkthrough: Pupils traditionally address a male teacher as 'sir', a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Desired is the past tense of desire, to wish for or want something.

clue.text: Workers in flexible steel make components

indicators.note: something flexible can be bent into another shape, so these letters are rearranged
one group is placed inside the other

blocks.note: the letters of this word rearranged
men are workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: Men working with bendable steel to produce parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Men as workers is an old crossword stand-by, from the phrase 'management and men'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elements are the basic constituent parts of a whole.

clue.text: Busy getting married?

blocks.note: first meaning: occupied, as a telephone line
second meaning: pledged to wed

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark suggests someone too occupied with wedding plans; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaged describes a phone line in use and a couple who have agreed to wed.

clue.text: Downgrading of French proposal

blocks.note: de is French for of
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: A French motion that lowers someone's rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotion is the act of reducing someone to a lower rank or position.

clue.text: Pass away when asleep in a drunken state

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about out of order, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dying in their sleep after a heavy night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass away' reads as dying, but it means time slipping by.
explanation.definitionFit: Time elapses when it goes by, so to elapse is for time to pass.

clue.text: Youngster with broken leg engulfed by depression

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are reassembled differently
being engulfed means swallowed up inside something else

blocks.note: a pit is a hollow or depression in the ground
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: A child with a fractured leg who has fallen into low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A piglet is a young pig, so it is a youngster of the animal kind.

clue.text: Financial backer has no part in disruption

indicators.note: disruption throws order into chaos, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An investor who keeps out of a troubled business.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a sponsor who supports an artist or cause with money.

clue.text: Wrong to show surprise as a result of jumping the gun

definitions.text: a result of jumping the gun

blocks.note: false means wrong or incorrect
to start is to jump in surprise

explanation.surface: Mistakenly flinching at an early shot in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping the gun means setting off before the starting signal, which in a race counts as an invalid beginning.

clue.text: Spent recklessly and sounded depressed

indicators.note: sounded tells us the word is heard rather than read

blocks.note: first meaning: squandered
feeling blue is feeling low

explanation.surface: Someone wasted their money and then sounded fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounded' also works on its own: blew is what you did to a horn.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow money is slang for wasting it extravagantly on something.

clue.text: It's tempting to have a morsel of food outside

definitions.note: a description of the thing, not a single word

indicators.note: the morsel goes around, on the outside of, the other piece

blocks.note: a bit is a small morsel to eat
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eating a snack out of doors is a temptation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A morsel' looks like one phrase, but the A is separate letters that the morsel wraps around.
explanation.definitionFit: Bait is a lure, food used to entice fish or prey, hence something tempting.

clue.text: Poor relations get in the way

indicators.note: one group goes inside the other

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Penniless relatives become an obstacle.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being skint means being broke, so it is an informal synonym for poor.

clue.text: Their use of me is quite excessive!

definitions.text: Their use of me is quite excessive!

blocks.clueFragment: Their use of me is quite excessive!
blocks.note: surface reading: a complaint that people make too much use of the speaker
setter's reading: the word me itself, a pronoun that self-centred people overuse

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like someone feeling exploited; really it is about people who say 'me' too often.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-obsessed people constantly talk about themselves, so they say the first-person pronoun far too much.
